# CalEvents

CalEvents is a public UC Berkeley campus events discovery site. It aggregates upcoming events from campus calendars and public source feeds, normalizes them into a single event feed, and refreshes automatically every morning.

## Primary Resources

- [Homepage](https://cal-events.com/): Search and browse upcoming Berkeley events by date, category, topic, source, and keyword.
- [For Agents](https://cal-events.com/for-agents.html): Human-readable agent entry point (tools, URL schema, CRUD limits).
- [Events JSON](https://cal-events.com/events.json): Public machine-readable event feed. The top-level object contains `events`, `sources`, `lastUpdated`, and `topic_vocabulary`.
- [Search Index](https://cal-events.com/search-index.json): Compact text-search index generated from the published events.
- [Feed Status](https://cal-events.com/status.json): Machine-readable ingestion status, source health, fallback usage, duplicate counts, and filtering counts.
- [OpenAPI Description](https://cal-events.com/openapi.json): API description for public static data resources.
- [API Catalog](https://cal-events.com/.well-known/api-catalog): Linkset catalog for API discovery.
- [Agent Skills](https://cal-events.com/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json): Skill files for search, status, detail, calendar export, and share.
- [Agent Card](https://cal-events.com/.well-known/agent-card.json): A2A agent card with the WebMCP and OpenAPI interfaces.
- [MCP Server Card](https://cal-events.com/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json): Browser WebMCP tool list and four named prompts. There is no remote MCP endpoint.

## Event Feed Shape

Each event in `events.json` has:

- `id`: stable source-derived event id
- `title`: event title
- `organizer`: organizer or campus unit
- `date`: first upcoming Pacific date in `YYYY-MM-DD`
- `end_date`: multi-day events only, the last Pacific date the event occurs
- `dates`: multi-day events only, every upcoming Pacific date the event occurs
- `time`: display time
- `end_time`: single-day timed events only, the Pacific end time in the same format as `time`, when the source gives one
- `location`: venue or location text
- `description`: event summary
- `tags`: primary category first, with optional secondary tags
- `topics`: zero to three published topic slugs; independent of `tags`
- `url`: official source URL
- `source`: normalized source id such as `livewhale`, `bampfa`, `calbears`, `cal_performances`, `haas`, `berkeley_law`, `simons`, `luma`, `begin`, `ai_risk`, `brsl`, or `cltc`. Call `list_filter_options` for the current list.

## Categories

Supported user-facing categories are `Academic`, `Arts`, `Sports`, `Science & Tech`, `Student Life`, and `Entrepreneurship`.

Topic slugs, labels, groups, and synonyms are published in
`events.json.topic_vocabulary.topics`. Agents must validate topic filters
against that block instead of assuming a fixed enum.

## URL Workspace Schema

Humans and agents share the same homepage query string:

| Param | Values | Role |
|-------|--------|------|
| `q` | string | Search query |
| `date` | `today` \| `tomorrow` \| `week` \| `upcoming` | Date bucket (default: week) |
| `category` | category name | Primary tag filter |
| `topic` | published topic slug | Topic filter, independent of category |
| `source` | source id | Source filter |
| `event` | event id | Selected detail |

WebMCP helpers: `build_calevents_url`, `get_ui_state`, `apply_ui_state`.

`apply_ui_state` replaces the whole view by default. Pass `mode: "merge"` to change only some fields, `reset: true` for the default view, or `event: null` to close the detail panel. An unknown value or event id returns `applied: false`. In merge mode that includes a stale event id already in the URL, and a URL the visitor changed during the call. Call `get_ui_state`, then retry. A `date` you pass stays in the URL, so a date word in `q` cannot override it. Then call `get_ui_state` and read `view` for what the page shows: the effective date range, chips, result count, and visible event ids. Read it again while `view.pending` is true.

Chip dismissal is search-only. Pass `dismiss` to `search_berkeley_events`. `apply_ui_state` has no dismiss field, and the page clears dismissed chips whenever its URL changes.

## WebMCP Tools (homepage)

Primitives (capability, not multi-step workflows): `search_berkeley_events` (ranked UI path), `get_event_by_id`, `generate_event_ics`, `get_cal_events_feed_status`, `get_ui_state`, `apply_ui_state`, `build_calevents_url`, `get_event_directions`, `list_filter_options` (valid categories, sources, date presets, topic slugs). Named outcomes live in MCP prompts and agent skills.

These tools run only in a browser tab on the homepage. An unknown category, source, topic, or date preset is an error, and so is a `startDate` or `endDate` that is not `YYYY-MM-DD`. A retired source such as `callink` is not accepted. `"All"` in any case clears a category or source.

`search_berkeley_events` reads date words in the query ("tomorrow", "this weekend") when you pass no date input. With no date at all it searches every upcoming day. A query's today or tomorrow widens to the week when that day has no match, as in the UI. A `datePreset` you pass never widens. Each result reports:

- `interpretations`: the chips the query set, each with a `key` and `label`. Pass keys in `dismiss` to drop them, like the chip's "x" in the UI.
- `effectiveDateRange`: the range searched, with `basis` (input, query, or default), `requested`, and `widened`.
- `relaxed` and `fallbackMessage`: set when nothing matched and the engine dropped a filter (weekend, category, or topic). Tell the user which one.
- `total`, `offset`, `limit`: page with `offset` while `offset` is below `total`.

## Privacy

Recent searches stay in the visitor's browser storage. No tool or file exposes them to agents, and that is on purpose.

## CRUD Limits

CalEvents is **read-only**. Events and feed status cannot be created, updated, or deleted through this site or its OpenAPI surface. Calendar `.ics` / Google Calendar URLs and directions links are derived reads.

## Guidance For Agents

- Prefer `events.json` for event data instead of scraping the rendered UI.
- Prefer WebMCP `search_berkeley_events` over ad-hoc substring filters when the homepage is available.
- Use `status.json` to understand freshness and source-level health.
- Dates are intended for America/Los_Angeles.
- Match a date window against `dates` when an event has it. `date` is only its first upcoming day.
- For a window that starts today, drop a single-day event whose `end_time` has passed on the Pacific clock. The UI hides it.
- Use official event `url` values for final user-facing citations or handoff links.
- Do not treat fallback/degraded source status as user-facing copy unless `data_quality_blocked` is true.
